data.name: Ministry of Investment (MISA)
documentation_sections: Approved activities list and sector eligibility
data.verification_method: Reviewed MISA Investor Guide, 12th Edition, July 2025 (misa.gov.sa/app/uploads/2025/07/Investor-Guide_12-04.pdf)
data.notes: Primary body for foreign investor registration in Saudi Arabia. Under the Investment Law (Royal Decree M/19, August 2024) and its Implementing Regulations (Ministerial Decision 1086, February 2025), foreign investors obtain an Investment Registration — the former activity-specific Foreign Investment License no longer exists. A single registration now covers multiple sectors. For most foreign investors, this registration precedes commercial registration. Formerly known as SAGIA (Saudi Arabian General Investment Authority) until 2020. Reference: MISA Investor Guide, 12th Edition (July 2025).

data.name: Qiwa — Labor Market Platform
documentation_sections: Employee transfer, exit, and flexible work permits
data.verification_method: Reviewed qiwa.sa platform pages and HRSD announcements (2025). Employer registration confirmed free of charge. Platform statistics (14.5M users, 11M contracts H1 2025) per HRSD published data.
data.notes: Official Saudi labor market platform operated by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (HRSD). Employer registration on Qiwa is mandatory before hiring any employees — this must be completed before the first worker joins. Registration is free. Key functions: employment contract authentication (all private-sector contracts must be authenticated via Qiwa), Nitaqat (Saudization) compliance monitoring, work permit management, and employee transfer processing. As of H1 2025: 14.5 million registered users, 11 million employment contracts processed. Platform URL: qiwa.sa (not qiwa.com.sa — the .com.sa domain redirects).

data.name: Muqeem — Residency and Expatriate Management Portal
data.name_alt: مقيم — بوابة إدارة الإقامة والعمالة الوافدة
documentation_sections: Exit visa and exit/re-entry visa management
2026 digital Iqama card delivery via Wasil
data.verification_method: Reviewed muqeem.sa portal and MOI/Jawazat fee schedules (2025). Iqama fees (SAR 51.75/year per employee), final exit visa (SAR 70), and exit/re-entry extension (SAR 103) confirmed against official Muqeem fee tables. 90-day Iqama deadline and late penalty schedule confirmed via HRSD/Jawazat published guidance.
data.notes: Official portal for managing Iqama (residency permits) and related visa services for expatriate employees in Saudi Arabia. Operated under the General Directorate of Passports (Jawazat), Ministry of Interior. Mandatory for employers sponsoring foreign staff. Key facts: (1) Iqama must be issued within 90 days of the employee's arrival in KSA — failure triggers penalties: SAR 500 (first offense), SAR 1,000 (second offense), then deportation proceedings. (2) Iqama fee: SAR 51.75 per employee per year (paid by the employer). (3) Final exit visa fee: SAR 70 per transaction. (4) Exit/re-entry visa extension: SAR 103 per transaction. (5) From 2026: Iqama renewal is fully digital; physical card replaced by Wasil card (digital identity card), delivered within 5 business days of renewal.

data.name: Economic Cities and Special Zones Authority (ECZA)
documentation_sections: Special Economic Zone regulations and investor guides
data.verification_method: Reviewed ECZA official website and Ministerial Resolution No. 468 (Official Gazette, 16 January 2026) confirming SEZ tax incentive framework: 5% CIT for 20 years, 0% WHT, 0% intra-zone VAT, 0% customs on capital equipment, 100% foreign ownership, 5-year Nitaqat relaxation.
data.notes: Sole governing authority for all five Saudi Special Economic Zones (SEZs): King Abdullah Economic City SEZ, Jazan SEZ, Ras Al-Khair SEZ, Cloud Computing SEZ, and Special Integrated Logistics Zone (SILZ). The foundational legal basis for SEZ tax incentives is Ministerial Resolution No. 468, published in the Official Gazette on 16 January 2026. Key distinction: all entities in industrial SEZs pay CIT (not Zakat) regardless of ownership nationality — opposite of mainland Saudi Arabia.
